items.title: Toronto Sandwich Shop and Nigerian-Inspired Eatery Lead October's New Restaurant Openings in the Area
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga, Brampton, Oshawa and Ajax saw several new restaurants open in October 2026. The outlet reports Vero Italian Sandwich Co., a Toronto shop known for its oversized sandwiches and freshly baked bread, opened a location inside the food court at Square One Shopping Centre. According to insauga.com, the sandwiches are built with imported Italian ingredients, specialty cheeses and cured meats, using bread made through a lengthy fermentation process. The outlet also reports a Toronto restaurant known for modern takes on Nigerian street food opened a new location in downtown Brampton, bringing suya-grilled meats, loaded rice bowls and Afro-fusion burgers to the area. According to insauga.com, the opening is part of a broader wave of new restaurants across the region last month, as Mississauga and its neighbouring cities continue adding to their dining scenes.

items.title: OPP Says Four Young People from Mississauga, Brampton and Milton Died in Puslinch Crash
items.summary: According to Wellington County OPP, four young people from Mississauga, Brampton and Milton died in a single-vehicle crash in Puslinch Township early Saturday morning. Police identified those killed as a 19-year-old man from Mississauga, a 19-year-old man from Brampton, a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga and a 15-year-old girl from Milton. OPP say two other young women from Mississauga, ages 17 and 16, survived, with the 17-year-old remaining in hospital with life-altering injuries and the 16-year-old suffering non-life-threatening injuries. According to police, six people were in the vehicle when it left the road, struck a guardrail and went into a ravine, with four pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators say they are reviewing all available evidence, including speed and seatbelt use, to determine what happened. In a social media video, police offered their condolences to the families and friends of those affected, and said multiple OPP units along with Victim Services Wellington-Guelph assisted with the response.

items.title: Dundas Street Logs Most Assaults as Peel Police Tally 308 Incidents in October
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police data, officers recorded 308 assaults across Mississauga and Brampton between Oct. 1 and Oct. 31, averaging close to 10 incidents a day region-wide. The data shows Mississauga accounted for 158 of those assaults and Brampton 149, with one additional incident logged at Humber College just across the Peel border in Toronto. Police reports show Dundas Street saw the most incidents in Mississauga, with 15 assaults along the busy east-west corridor, while Ann Street in Port Credit recorded four and the City Centre area near Square One and Celebration Square recorded three. In Brampton, police say Hurontario Street, which runs through both cities, logged seven assaults, followed by three each on Bovaird Drive and Queen Street. According to the data, assaults can range from threats and minor altercations to attacks causing serious injury, and the figures do not show how many incidents led to arrests or charges.

items.title: Mississauga Campaign Spent Over $100,000 on Viral Ads to Fuel Tedjo's Mayoral Upset
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Alvin Tedjo's mayoral campaign spent more than $100,000 on social media ads, part of a strategy behind what the outlet calls the biggest election-night upset in the GTA over both the sitting and a former Mississauga mayor. The paper reports the campaign's social team worked from a basement office nicknamed the Ministry of Content, tracking ad performance on Post-it notes and finding food-related videos consistently outperformed others. Deputy campaign manager Kelly Singh told the Star the team was flabbergasted as the results came in and still isn't certain what tipped the race. According to the Star, staff point to several factors working together: affordability and safety messaging, an aggressive social push, and in-person events from a pickleball court to Ridgeway Plaza. The outlet says the office keeps hand-drawn Ted Lasso-style Believe signs, after an original cardboard version by deputy communications director Kris Pangilinan was later replicated by Tedjo's sister. According to the Star, the campaign closed with an all-hands get-out-the-vote push on election day.

items.title: Peel Police Seek Public's Help Finding Boy Last Seen Near South Service Road
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, officers are asking the public for help locating a 13-year-old boy who went missing in Mississauga. Police say he was last seen Friday evening near South Service Road and Hurontario Street. According to investigators, he is described as five-foot-three with a medium build and short black hair. Police say he was last seen wearing all black clothing along with a camouflage-print North Face jacket and was carrying a navy blue Jordan backpack. According to Peel Regional Police, anyone with information on his whereabouts is asked to call 905-453-2121, extension 1133, and reference incident number PR260369529.

items.title: Mississauga Whistleblower Program to Add Fraud and Waste Hotline by Early 2027
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the City of Mississauga plans to launch an expanded Whistleblower Program in early 2027 that will let residents confidentially report suspected fraud, waste or wrongdoing at the municipality. The outlet reports a dedicated fraud and waste hotline is expected to be in place within the first three months of the year, giving both city employees and the public an independent and confidential way to raise concerns. According to a staff report cited by insauga.com, complaints will first be assessed by a team drawn from the internal audit, legal services and human resources departments, which will then decide whether to investigate internally or bring in an external investigator. The outlet says cases involving senior officials, such as the city manager or a commissioner, would likely be handed to an outside investigator to preserve independence. According to insauga.com, the city created its original Whistleblower Program in 2014, and internal audit director Amy Truong said in the staff report that it has supported accountability and ethical conduct for the past decade.

items.title: TikTok Video Spotlights Food World Plus's Chocolate and Snack Selection in Mississauga
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, the newly opened Food World Plus at 50 Matheson Blvd. is drawing shoppers in part for its extensive chocolate, candy and snack selection. The outlet reports the 176,000-square-foot multicultural grocery store stocks items from Europe, the Caribbean, the Middle East, East Asia and South Asia, along with a Costco-style warehouse section for bulk buying. Mississauga.com says the store also offers parking for 1,100 vehicles. The outlet quotes a TikTok user, @KirbyCub, who wrote that visiting the store changed their view of Mississauga as a tourist destination. According to mississauga.com, the store's size and variety have made it a draw for shoppers well beyond the immediate neighbourhood since it opened.

items.title: Credit Valley Conservation Nears Completion of First Watershed Plan Update Since 1956
items.summary: According to Credit Valley Conservation, the agency is in the final stages of a multi-year update to its Credit River Watershed plan, the first since the original document was created in 1956. CVC says the river runs roughly 90 kilometres from the northern Greater Toronto Area to its mouth in south Mississauga, and the plan covers the watershed across Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon and several other communities including Orangeville, Halton Hills and parts of Dufferin County. The agency reports the update draws on current science and data along with input from partners, stakeholders and the community to set long-term priorities for CVC and its municipal partners. According to CVC, a watershed plan serves as a tool for understanding the past and planning for the future health of the watershed. The agency says the new version is meant to guide its scope of work for years to come, reflecting decades of change across the region since the plan was first drafted nearly 70 years ago.

items.title: Natural Resources Canada Names Paul Coffey Arena Its Building of the Year
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Natural Resources Canada has named Paul Coffey Arena its Energy Star Building of the Year, recognizing the Malton facility named for the Mississauga-born Hockey Hall of Fame member. The city says upgrades to lighting, building controls and arena equipment, backed by better performance data, have helped the facility use less energy and cost less to operate. Anna Cascioli, the city's director of facilities and property management, said the recognition reflects the practical work of teams making municipal buildings more efficient and affordable to run. According to the city, the arena was formerly known as Malton Arena and continues to serve the community through Learn to Skate, ice hockey, public skating, ball hockey and other recreation programs. The city reports the award adds to a growing list of ENERGY STAR-certified municipal facilities as Mississauga works toward its long-term climate and energy goals.

items.title: Shelter Fees Drop to $25 for Dogs and Cats During Mississauga Adopt-a-thon
items.summary: According to an Oct. 29 news release from Mississauga Animal Services, the city is cutting its adoption fees to $25 for dogs and cats during a two-week Adopt-a-thon running from Nov. 2 to Nov. 14. The release says those fees normally run $280 for a dog and $190 for a cat, with the discounted $25 price still subject to tax and any applicable pet licence fees. Mississauga Animal Services says the event runs Monday through Saturday at the shelter, where prospective adopters can meet animals currently available, including a dog named Messi. The service says the offer is open to anyone interested in adopting, not just Mississauga residents, as it looks to find homes for more animals. According to the release, standard adoption pricing returns once the Adopt-a-thon window closes on Nov. 14.
